searchText: > Interestingly beaconcha.in says I've lost nearly 32 ETH - I wonder if it thinks I started with 64ETH because this validator had to make two deposits (one of which was invalid): https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/validator/846af35f93ee70c5a9136a1bcbebcf52afaf931028562466f09f1689632fbbf60f809fd791d0c5dc44b45f1474988683 <@!340345049063882753> just saw this ..."income" is not working properly atm, please ignore 😦 noobie q: before starting beacon node and validator node, I believe I need to start geth client base. My q is: do i start my geth pointed to goerli or to mainnet eth chain/instance? thx! For Schlesi, be sure to use Goerli as your Eth1 network! gotcha, thx could anyone spare 10-50k göETH? wanna try and start some more validators on schlesi Fair warning: the validator count is currently rather low, and so there will be a low churn rate, deposits are slow, and you'll be the majority validator of a devnet. 😛 you mean i can break it all by myself? i am good at that ok, i ll work my way to 50 validators or thereabouts, not in any rush, but need to experiment a bit, and low validator schlesi seems appropriate post your address more validators are certainly welcome but try not to run more than ~30% maybe to keep it balanced, what do you think? IMHO we should plan towards a restart with larger validator count from the start The devnet right now is great though, I'm syncing 4 different clients 🙂 5, if you count occasional lodestar experiments They are catching up, sync is looking better every day 🎉 Synced Nimbus almost to the head of the schlesi chain! And made experimental Eth2stats support (after adding some API endpoints to the already experimental nimbus API) I didn't have success yet What magic did you use? 🙂 I went through so many hoops and weird issues to get here, it's not even funny. But everything has been merged upstream into nimbus devel and eth2stats client, so you should be able to pull this off One issue I had though is the low peer count. It seemed to like two of my schlesi nodes better, so I changed the bootnodes And there are strange ways you can induce crashes through API calls and the weird UDP spam from earlier, but it seems good now. ``` --data-dir="/data" --web3-url=wss:// some address here --bootstrap-file="/data/custom_bootnodes.txt" --udp-port=9000 --tcp-port=9000 --listen-address=0.0.0.0 --nat="extip:{{public_ip_address}}" --log-level="DEBUG" --deposit-contract=0xA15554BF93a052669B511ae29EA21f3581677ac5 --state-snapshot="/root/genesis.ssz" --rpc --rpc-port=4000 --rpc-address=127.0.0.1 ``` Is what I use to run nimbus currently. And in a docker image I built, adapted from the thing in the repo, but on my own branch with api fixes (before it was merged) and pulling in build data to not redo the complete build. <@!203220829473996800>, is the `nat` parameter above being replaced by a template engine of some sort? If you are behind a router, the `extip:...` option should indicate the IP address of the router It's a template yes I use ansible ok, I see I've extensive configuration setup for auto-assign validators, docker deployments, automated provisioning etc. all managed through ansible. I may publish some of it, but with all the experimentation it's hard to keep it consistent at times, so it may need some polishing. Shared for 4 different clients, and soon with Lodestar as well 🙂 The nat feature and auto-discover stuff of nimbus is cool, but I'm setting the ip manually since I've had problems in the past. Docker containers break things, with Prysm it didn't work. Is your Dockerfile much different from ours? Not too different. I just `ADD` in my local nimbus install, instead of cloning it. And then add some schlesi data such as genesis file for convenience, and tag it my way to push it up to dockerhub and deploy where I like One problem is that I've set up automated validator assignments for that key standard mentioned earlier here. But only enabled it for Prysm. The other clients all have their own format one way or another, and I don't have tooling yet to convert validator key formats. If a client can support the key format, I'll start running validators with them 🙂 I guess you are referring to this spec: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2335 Yep, lost the eip number for a bit, that one yes I'm pretty sure we fully support this in Teku. Great, send me some links and I'll look into running validators on Teku. excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: And there are strange ways you can induce crashes through API calls and the weird UDP spam from earlier, but it seems good now.

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
```
  --data-dir="/data"
  --web3-url=wss:// some address here
  --bootstrap-file="/data/custom_bootnodes.txt"
  --udp-port=9000
  --tcp-port=9000
  --listen-address=0.0.0.0
  --nat="extip:{{public_ip_address}}"
  --log-level="DEBUG"
  --deposit-contract=0xA15554BF93a052669B511ae29EA21f3581677ac5
  --state-snapshot="/root/genesis.ssz"
  --rpc --rpc-port=4000 --rpc-address=127.0.0.1
```
Is what I use to run nimbus currently. And in a docker image I built, adapted from the thing in the repo, but on my own branch with api fixes (before it was merged) and pulling in build data to not redo the complete build.
